name: SCOOB-II
mission: SCOOB-II is the second satellite in NTU's Student Satellite Series, aiming to provide real-world satellite learning opportunities for engineering undergraduates. It carries a high-power electronic payload to demonstrate advanced electronics test operations in space.
equipment: SCOOB-II is equipped with an advanced electronics payload for testing operations in space, an improved attitude determination and control system (ADCS) for sun-pointing capabilities, and two deployable solar panels to enhance power generation.
adcs: The satellite's ADCS includes two Fine Sun Sensors (FSS), two Coarse Sun Sensors (CSS), a 3-axis magnetometer, three magnetorquers (MTQ), and three reaction wheels (RW), achieving a determination accuracy of less than 5 degrees.
payload: The satellite's payload includes advanced electronics for testing operations in space, supported by an improved ADCS and deployable solar panels for enhanced power generation.
manufacturer: Satellite Research Centre (SaRC), Nanyang Technological University (NTU)
shape: Rectangular box with deployable solar panels

name: ARCADE
mission: ARCADE (Atmospheric Coupling and Dynamics Explorer) is a scientific microsatellite developed to study the equatorial ionosphere and mesosphere-lower thermosphere (MLT) region. It aims to provide insights into atmospheric coupling processes and the dynamics of the equatorial ionosphere.
equipment: The satellite is equipped with four instruments: an imager for atmospheric gravity waves, a plasma probe for measuring ionospheric plasma density and velocity, an atomic oxygen instrument to study material degradation in low Earth orbit, and an optical imager for Earth observation.
adcs: The Attitude Determination and Control System (ADCS) comprises 12 coarse sun sensors, Inertial Measurement Units (IMUs), a star tracker, three magnetorquers, and three reaction wheels.
